questions.q: What shift does the summary say we are living through right now?
a: From the Industrial Age to the Information Age
From capitalism back to a barter economy
From farming to hunting and gathering
From democracy to corporate rule
questions.why: The overview calls this the greatest evolutionary event in history, replacing the old school-college-job blueprint.

questions.q: What does the summary say schools teach you about money?
a: They train you to handle it poorly and stay an employee
They give you a thorough financial education
They encourage students to start businesses
They teach investing better than parents do
questions.why: Lesson 1 says schools push an employee mindset and never teach the basics of finance.

questions.q: What are the four asset categories listed in the summary?
a: Businesses, real estate, paper assets, commodities
Stocks, bonds, savings, pensions
Wages, bonuses, tips, commissions
Property, cars, jewelry, art
questions.why: Lesson 2 names businesses, real estate, paper assets and commodities, with examples for each.

questions.q: What does the summary advise doing before picking an asset class?
a: Take stock of your income, expenses, assets and liabilities
Pay off every debt you owe first
Wait until you are earning a large salary
Ask a bank to manage your money for you
questions.why: Lesson 2 says to review your finances with an income statement and balance sheet before starting to learn.

questions.q: When does the summary say taking on debt makes sense?
a: When you use it to buy assets that earn more than the interest
When the interest rate is fixed rather than variable
When you use it to buy a new car or television
When it helps you pay for a university degree
questions.why: Lesson 3 says debt is fine as long as the asset it buys produces more income than you owe.
